slides.title: Why the margin fell
Promotions, e-commerce and shrink, not wages, explain 87% of the operating margin Harlow lost since FY2023

claims.claim: 86.7% of the margin decline comes from promotions, e-commerce fulfillment and shrink
evidence: Waterfall: FY2023 3.37%; Promotional mix −0.70 pp; Shrink −0.50 pp; Private label +0.18 pp; Store labor −0.30 pp; Occupancy and energy −0.20 pp; E-commerce fulfillment −0.84 pp; FY2025 1.02%

claims.claim: Promotional mix: 5 more percentage points of sales sold on promotion, each earning 14 percentage points less
E-commerce fulfillment: grew from 0.4% to 1.2% of sales as online orders nearly tripled
Shrink: up from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales, worst in the leanest-staffed stores
Store labor: only 0.3 percentage points, the smallest cost line that rose
evidence: Promotional mix = change in share × 14 percentage points lower margin; private label = change in share × 12 percentage points higher. Part of the shrink rise reflects thinner staffing (p. 9)

slides.title: Fewer hours per sales dollar offset most of the 9.4% wage rise; labor cost grew just 0.3 percentage points of sales

claims.claim: Management's diagnosis is right about the rate
evidence: 9.4% average hourly wage including benefits
From $16.80 to $18.38 an hour
Driven by the state minimum wage and a tight labor market
Another 4% minimum-wage rise arrives in 2027

claims.claim: Stores already run leaner than in FY2023
evidence: −5.98% labor hours per $1,000 of sales
From 7.02 to 6.60 hours per $1,000 of sales
Offset most of the higher hourly rate
In the leanest stores, receiving checks and produce rotation now get skipped on busy days

claims.claim: The net effect on margin is small
evidence: 0.3 pp change in store labor as a share of sales
From 11.8% to 12.1% of sales
Labor cost rose $14.3M, the largest increase in dollars
But $9.8M of that simply followed sales growth

slides.title: Promotions are buying volume at a loss: their share of sales rose to 29%, yet 38% of FY2025 events lost money

claims.claim: Promotional sales gained 5 percentage points of sales in two years
evidence: +5 pp
Promotional share: FY2023 24%; FY2024 26.2%; FY2025 29%
Depth raised to hold traffic against ValuMart

claims.claim: Many events no longer pay, and vendors fund less of them
evidence: 38% of FY2025 events lost money after counting the extra units sold
46% of markdowns paid by vendors, down from 55% in FY2023
Harlow now pays more of every markdown

claims.claim: The category team's point that the deepest-promotion stores grew comparable sales 1.8%, against 0.2%, shows volume, not profit

slides.title: Counted fully, e-commerce loses about $10M a year: the team's reported profit leaves out delivery and cannibalized sales

claims.claim: E-commerce net contribution is −$10.4M a year
evidence: Contribution of new sales $7.7M; Picking −$9.8M; Third-party delivery −$10.7M; Delivery fees +$2.4M; Net contribution −$10.4M
$127.8M online sales, FY2025 × 30% new to Harlow (survey) × 20% contribution per new dollar − $18.1M fulfillment cost (finance) = −$10.4M net contribution a year

claims.claim: 22.5% of third-party delivery cost is recovered through delivery fees
New sales: customers say 70% of what they buy online would otherwise have been bought in a Harlow store
evidence: New share from a survey of 2,300 online customers; 20 cents a dollar is finance's estimate

claims.claim: Third-party delivery: the largest cost, booked by finance outside the team's 6.1% margin
Growth: each extra order adds to the loss, so a freeze limits the damage but does not end it

slides.title: Why the labor cut is the wrong first move
Shrink rises as staffing thins, with the leanest quarter of stores losing 3.1% of sales against 2.3% in the best-staffed

claims.claim: Thin staffing shows up as waste and receiving errors
evidence: Shrink by staffing quartile: Q1 (fewest hours) 3.1%; Q2 2.7%; Q3 2.4%; Q4 (most hours) 2.3%
Chain, FY2025 2.6%
Q1 (fewest hours): managers say produce rotation and receiving checks are skipped on busy days
Mix: fresh waste and receiving errors are 65% of shrink, the parts that need staff time
Trend: chain shrink rose from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales as hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6%

claims.claim: $2.3M expected gain from shrink controls in Q1 and Q2, FY2028
evidence: Quartiles of the 58 stores; the expected gain assumes each quartile carries a quarter of sales and that the hours come from the most-staffed stores

slides.title: Net of shrink and the 2027 wage rise, management's labor plan leaves FY2028 operating income near today's, at $16M

claims.claim: Management's plan leaves FY2028 operating income at $15.7M; 1.0% of sales
evidence: $15.3M operating income, FY2025 − $7.3M 2027 minimum-wage rise: 4% on today's $181.9M store labor − $0.3M delivery provider's proposed 3% rise + $14.5M management's estimate for 8% fewer store hours − $6.5M extra shrink from thinner staffing = $15.7M

claims.claim: Even on generous assumptions, the cut nets about $8.0M and fixes none of the bigger causes
evidence: Shrink responds to hours as in FY2023–25, when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6.0% and shrink rose 0.5 percentage points
Only fresh waste and receiving errors, 65% of shrink, respond to staffing; theft does not
Customer response to longer checkout waits and stock-outs is not counted, so this is a best case
E-commerce frozen at its FY2025 size, still losing about $10M a year; promotions unchanged

claims.claim: The labor plan targets the smallest cause of the decline and gives back almost half its saving in shrink

slides.title: Five moves on the real causes
Bringing promotions back to their FY2023 share would add about $6M a year, even after the volume it loses

claims.claim: Promotions reset adds $6.4M more operating income a year
evidence: 5 pp of sales taken off promotion, from 29.0% back to 24.0% × 9 pp net gain per dollar: 75% × 14 pp kept, less 25% × 6 cents lost × $1,411.9M FY2028 sales after store exits and the fee change = $6.4M

claims.claim: Less than half of the loss-making promotional volume has to go
evidence: Loss-making events carried about 11 percentage points of sales (38% of events × 29.0%, if events are of similar size); this wave removes 5
Three-quarters of the removed sales are bought at regular price, gaining 14 percentage points; a quarter is lost at 6 cents a dollar
Promotional depth stays in the 11 ValuMart trade areas, where traffic is most at risk
Vendor funding, down from 55% to 46% of markdowns, is renegotiated but not counted

claims.claim: Each point of promotional share left in place costs about $1.3M a year
evidence: The lost-volume share is our assumption: the pack has no lift data

slides.title: The tested delivery fee, rolled out chain-wide, would save about $2.5M a year for a 2% dip in online sales

claims.claim: Shoppers switch to click-and-collect
evidence: Fee test change in test stores: Average fee per delivered order +106.45%; Click-and-collect orders +14%; Total e-commerce sales −2%; Delivered orders −9%
Click-and-collect: absorbs most lost deliveries, so total online sales barely move

claims.claim: Operating income gained a year $2.5M
evidence: Fulfillment cost saved a year $3M: $18.1M today − $15.1M at test volumes and fees
Contribution lost on lower online sales −$0.5M: −2% × $127.8M × 20 cents, all assumed lost

claims.claim: Pays while online sales fall less than about 12%. Each delivered order still costs $7.40 more than its fee
evidence: Test: $7.99 fee, $100 threshold, four stores, ten weeks

slides.title: Exiting the nine loss-making stores would add about $6.6M a year; six leases lapse by 2027 with no board vote needed

claims.claim: Exiting the nine stores adds $6.6M more operating income a year
evidence: $3.1M four-wall EBITDA losses removed + $118M sales of the nine stores × 25% that move to a nearby Harlow store (past closures) × 12% contribution on moved sales = $6.6M

claims.claim: The three early exits are the only call the board must make
evidence: Losses and sales spread evenly across the nine, so the six lapsing leases bring about $4.4M and the three long leases $2.2M
The three early exits cost $7.5M once and pay back in about 3.4 years; they use $7.5M of the $25M cap
Overhead stays; closed stores' wage rise and depreciation are not counted, so the gain is conservative

claims.claim: Keeping the three long-lease stores would cost the plan $2.2M a year; a payback of about 3.4 years justifies the vote
evidence: Store-level split of losses not in the briefing pack; the even split is our assumption

slides.title: Private label is a cheaper value signal than deeper promotions; holding today's pace adds about $3.8M by FY2028

claims.claim: A value signal that adds margin instead of costing it
evidence: ValuMart: stores within three miles of its 11 new stores lost 4.2% of comparable sales, against growth of 1.1% elsewhere
Price image: 41% of shoppers now call Harlow more expensive, up from 33% in FY2023, despite deeper promotions
Margin: each share point in private label earns 12 percentage points more, where promotion costs 14

claims.claim: Expected gain by FY2028 $3.8M
evidence: 18.5% private-label share, FY2025 actual + 2.2 pp added FY2026–28: 0.75 pp a year, the FY2023–25 pace, × 3 years = 20.8% share in FY2028
2.25 pp of sales × 12 pp margin premium × $1,412M
Product development and packaging cost is not in the briefing pack; it falls under the $25M cap

slides.title: Together, the five moves would add about $22M a year by FY2028, and store exits and promotions bring most of it

claims.claim: The five moves add $21.6M a year by FY2028
evidence: 1 Cut loss-making promotions, 38% of events; spare ValuMart areas: $6.4M
2 Exit the nine stores with negative four-wall EBITDA: $6.6M
3 Grow private label, worth 12 percentage points more margin: $3.8M
4 Restore receiving and rotation where shrink hits 3.1% of sales: $2.3M
5 Roll out the $7.99 fee and $100 threshold chain-wide: $2.5M
Total $21.6M

claims.claim: Promotions and the delivery fee need no capital; of the sized moves, only the three early store exits use the $25M cap

slides.title: Sequence, cases and gates
With labor hours cut last, operating income would reach about $38M in FY2028, after $7M of known cost increases

claims.claim: Operating income would reach $37.8M in FY2028
evidence: $15.3M operating income, FY2025 + $21.6M five moves on the causes − $7.1M 2027 minimum-wage rise and delivery rate rise + $8.1M labor step: 8% fewer hours, net of shrink = $37.8M

claims.claim: The labor step comes last and is netted for the shrink it causes
evidence: Known cost increases: the 4% minimum-wage rise on FY2028 store labor ($6.8M) and the provider's proposed 3% ($0.3M)
Labor step: 8% fewer hours on the post-exit chain at 2027 wages saves $14.2M, less $6.1M of extra shrink
Prices, volumes and other costs held at FY2025 levels; FY2028 sales of $1,412M after exits and the fee change
Sales growth and vendor-funding recovery are upside not counted; cost trends other than the known increases are held flat, which flatters the base

slides.title: The plan lifts margin to about 2.7% by FY2028; reaching 3.0% needs a second, deeper promotion cut

claims.claim: The plan lifts margin to about 2.7% by FY2028
evidence: Operating margin: FY2025 actual 1.02%; Stress case, FY2028 2.113%; Base case, FY2028 2.68%
FY2028 target 3.0%

claims.claim: About $4.5M short of 3.0%, and promotions can close it
evidence: Further cut in promotional share that reaches 3.0%: 3.3 pp = ($4.5M − $0.3M flat delivery rate) ÷ $1.3M a point
Upside not counted: vendor funding, and about $2.8M for each 1% of new sales

claims.claim: Stress case: still double FY2025 and well above the 1.0% the labor plan would leave
evidence: 2.7% base case, FY2028 − 0.6 pp promotions at 26.2%, half-pace private label, more shrink = 2.1% stress case, FY2028

claims.claim: Margin without the labor step 2.1%
Both waves together remove about 8.3 of the roughly 11 percentage points of sales in loss-making events; the second starts only if sales near ValuMart hold

slides.title: Promotions and delivery fees go first, as they alone clear the FY2026 covenant; labor hours come last

claims.claim: Sequence of the six moves by fiscal half-year
evidence: 1 Promotions: Reset from Q2, 24% of sales; Second wave to about 21%, if ValuMart-area sales hold
5 Delivery fee: Chain-wide rollout; Run-rate; contract renewed
2 Store exits: Six leases lapse; three early exits
3 Private label: Plus 0.75 pp of sales a year
4 Shrink controls: Receiving and rotation restored in Q1–Q2 stores
6 Labor hours: 8% fewer hours, after the shrink gate
Milestones: Board vote on three early exits; Second-wave decision; Covenant: at least $20M; Shrink gate

claims.claim: Promotions and delivery fees alone clear the FY2026 covenant
evidence: $15.3M FY2025 base + $5.1M promotions reset, three quarters of a year + $1.9M delivery fee, three quarters of a year − $0.2M delivery rate rise = $22.02M FY2026, against the $20M covenant
FY2026 is the first plan year and the covenant year, as set out in the briefing pack; promotions and fees start in its second quarter

slides.title: Five gates tell the board early when to hold course, slow down or fall back

claims.claim: Promotional share of sales gate
evidence: Threshold: At or below 26.0% from FY2026 Q2, the level that still meets the covenant; Checked: Monthly from FY2026 Q2; If crossed: Bring part of the hours cut forward in the best-staffed stores; Verdict: The gate that protects the lender / Promotions carry the covenant in FY2026; if they lag, an early hours cut is the fallback

claims.claim: Comparable sales near ValuMart gate
evidence: Threshold: No worse than FY2025's −4.2%; Checked: Quarterly; If crossed: Restore depth there only and hold the second wave; Verdict: Guards the traffic the promotions defended

claims.claim: Online sales after the fee change gate
evidence: Threshold: A fall of less than about 12%, the break-even; Checked: 10 weeks after rollout; If crossed: Return to the $75 free-delivery threshold; Verdict: Tests the 4-store result at chain scale

claims.claim: Shrink in the two leanest quartiles gate
evidence: Threshold: At or below 2.4% of sales, today's Q3 level; Checked: FY2027 H2, before any hours cut; If crossed: Delay the labor step; Verdict: Proves the controls work before hours go

claims.claim: Chain shrink after the hours cut gate
evidence: Threshold: Not above FY2025's 2.6% of sales; Checked: Quarterly from FY2028; If crossed: Stop further cuts and restore receiving hours; Verdict: Stops the cut if shrink returns

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Fix promotions, delivery fees and weak stores now and cut hours last: promotions and delivery fees go first, as they alone clear the FY2026 covenant; exit the nine loss-making stores (board to vote on the three early exits, $7.5M one-time), grow private label, restore shrink controls, and cut labor hours 8% last, after the shrink gate; decide on a second promotion wave to about 21% of sales if sales near ValuMart hold, to reach 3.0%.

alternatives_considered.option: Management's 8% store-hours cut as the first move (labor plan)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected as first move: net of shrink and the 2027 wage rise it leaves FY2028 operating income near today's, at $16M (1.0% of sales); "targets the smallest cause of the decline and gives back almost half its saving in shrink". Kept as the last step, after the shrink gate.

alternatives_considered.option: Keeping the three long-lease stores (no early exits)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Would cost the plan $2.2M a year; a payback of about 3.4 years justifies the vote.

alternatives_considered.option: Deeper promotions as the value signal versus growing private label
alternatives_considered.treatment: Private label is a cheaper value signal than deeper promotions; each share point earns 12 pp more, where promotion costs 14.
A freeze limits the damage but does not end it.

alternatives_considered.option: Second, deeper promotion wave to about 21% of sales
alternatives_considered.treatment: Needed to reach 3.0%; decided in FY2027 H1, starts only if sales near ValuMart hold.

alternatives_considered.option: Bringing part of the hours cut forward in the best-staffed stores
alternatives_considered.treatment: Fallback if promotional share is above 26.0% from FY2026 Q2.
Fallback if online sales fall more than about 12% after the fee change.
